item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00161","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C04","C17"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C16 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. It establishes an ordered succession to a department secretary upon death or absence, begins with the Under Secretary and then the Assistant Secretaries, and includes a specific rule for determining rank by appointment date with a same-date tie-breaker. The child expands this same machinery across the Department of Defense and the three military departments, repeatedly using ordered lists and seniority by length of service. C04 and C17 also provide close list-based succession structures, but lack C16's additional ranking and tie-breaking machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"In the event of the death, disability, or absence of the Secretary of the Army, the following-designated officers shall succeed to the position of, and act as, Secretary of the Army in the order indicated: 1. Under Secretary of the Army. 2. Assistant Secretaries of the Army, in the order fixed by their length of service as such.","parent_excerpt":"The Under Secretary of the Interior shall perform the duties of the Secretary of the Interior in case of the death, resignation, absence, or sickness of the Secretary of the Interior. ... The ranking Assistant Secretary of the Interior present shall perform the duties ... in case of the death, resignation, absence, or sickness of both the Secretary ... and the Under Secretary.","explanation":"Both prescribe departmental succession triggered by the secretary's unavailability, placing the Under Secretary first and ranked Assistant Secretaries next."},{"child_excerpt":"Precedence within a particular group between or among two or more officers having the same date of appointment shall be as determined by the Secretary of Defense at the time of appointment.","parent_excerpt":"The Assistant Secretary of the Interior whose commission bears the earliest date, or, if the commissions of Assistant Secretaries bear the same date, the Assistant Secretary who first took the oath of office, shall be considered the ranking Assistant Secretary of the Interior","explanation":"Both use appointment chronology to rank officers and expressly provide machinery for resolving equal appointment dates, though the child changes the tie-breaking method."},{"child_excerpt":"the following-designated officers ... shall succeed ... in the order indicated","parent_excerpt":"The ranking Assistant Secretary ... shall perform the duties of the Secretary","explanation":"The child generalizes C16's hierarchical acting-secretary framework into repeated, expressly enumerated succession schedules."}]}
